meta.title: Omarchy Speed Leaderboard
meta.tagline: DHH called 50 seconds the Omarchy Quattro Install World Record. This is the book that keeps it.

runs.note: Declared by DHH as the Omarchy Quattro Install World Record.
The slow end of the range, and the clearest demonstration of why the drive is the variable that matters.

milestones.headline: Under five minutes, with a fast connection
milestones.body: DHH publishes the breakdown: one minute formatting and encrypting the drive, one minute installing Arch, two minutes forty installing and configuring Omarchy itself. The install still needs the network, so bandwidth is part of everyone's number.

milestones.headline: Under three minutes
milestones.body: Ryan Hughes rebuilds the install flow around a new offline ISO. Removing the network removes the largest source of variance between machines — from here on, an install time is a statement about your disk, not your ISP.

milestones.headline: Two minutes
milestones.body: Two days later, the same work lands at two minutes flat for a full install of a complete, configured operating system.

milestones.headline: Sub-minute becomes possible
milestones.body: The Quattro release notes claim installation is over 30% faster and the ISO more than a gigabyte smaller, at under 6GB — with sub-minute installs now possible. Days later, an HP ZBook Ultra G1a turns the claim into 50 seconds.

baselines.note: Core install on a modern NVMe SSD, before out-of-box setup, drivers and updates.
Full erase-and-reinstall on supported hardware, network dependent.
